# OBS002 `equivalence-statement`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

An `equivalence` statement.

## Why

`equivalence` makes different variables share storage, defeating type checking and optimisation
(aliasing). It is obsolescent since Fortran 2018. Use `transfer`, pointers, or separate variables.

## Reported

```fortran
equivalence (a, b)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
b = transfer(a, b)
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS002] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS002` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `OB012` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
